coverage_notes: Repeated records describe one project. The February 2023 listing date does not align cleanly with supplied July 2023 prices and later comparisons; version chronology is unresolved. Server-operation and summarized observation windows differ between twelve and six months. Main-text/appendix poisoning-percentage conversions conflict; retain 1,000-image counts and appendix outcomes of 6/10 and 9/10 rather than reconciling them inventively. Timing-bias direction is also inconsistent, although offset adjustment is clear. German, Chinese, and Czech checkpoints were unavailable; Tagalog lacked sufficient data. Additional protocol details include 500 DNS requests/second, price checks for only the top 10,000 domains per dataset, and six purchases per dataset. Historical domain-price analysis reports 0.01% control for under $60/year, excluding other operational costs. Transparency proposals and general Common Crawl defenses were not implemented or validated.

substance:
This collaboration seeks parameter extraction with polynomial query and execution complexity when an oracle reveals only class labels, not numerical outputs. Its cryptanalytic analogy treats public nonlinearities and secret linear parameters like known cipher operations surrounding secret keys. The objective is numerical parameter recovery up to unavoidable symmetries, not merely matching task accuracy. The threat model nevertheless grants known architecture, arbitrary real-valued queries, sufficiently precise arithmetic, and fully connected ReLU layers.

The central substitution for unavailable derivatives is geometric: find a class transition by binary search, then follow its decision-boundary patch until orientation changes. Such dual points lie on both a class boundary and an internal neuron’s critical hyperplane. Finite search approximates rather than exactly locates transitions. Extraction alternates signature recovery, identifying a hyperplane up to scale, and sign recovery, identifying its active side, layer by layer.

Signature recovery combines incomplete local observations through consistent linear equations. For deeper layers, rank tests account for shared zero coordinates from inactive ReLUs. SVD supplies numerical consistency diagnostics; maximal-clique clustering rejects isolated false edges, and a triple-consistency filter removes all observed false positives. Insufficient activation diversity sends the algorithm back to collect more dual points. Nearly inactive neurons make the final parameters expensive, with later layers potentially requiring millions of points.

Sign recovery replaces the predecessor’s exhaustive sign search with an explicitly heuristic statistical test. Distances walked along the decision boundary until later-layer neurons toggle proxy otherwise inaccessible output slopes; shorter distances provide evidence for the active side. Earlier-layer toggles cannot reflect the target neuron’s state and are excluded. The implemented middle variant continues through unwanted toggles, accumulating distance, but discards points that repeatedly encounter the same earlier neurons. White-box diagnostics test the mechanism and observe an average speed ratio around 1.2 rather than the rough theoretical 1.4. Hoeffding-based calculations assess vote imbalance against 50/50; difficult neurons receive fresh-input reruns.

The showcase CIFAR-10 network has hidden widths 256, 256, 256, and 64, approximately 935,000 parameters, and 52% test accuracy. Target-layer experiments use 64-bit arithmetic but assume perfectly recovered preceding layers. Reported parameter precision is usually at least 18 bits under that condition. Crucially, approximately 16-hour signature timing excludes pairwise clustering that could take weeks, and symbolic gradients accelerate a component otherwise intended to use label queries. Approximately 8.5-hour sign timing assumes dual points and boundary normals already exist and uses a 256-core server. Thus the evidence demonstrates constituent extraction methods, not a completed hard-label-only end-to-end runtime or accumulated-error result. A usable optimized black-box implementation is explicitly deferred.
attribution_limits: These are collaborative methods, interpretations, and scope decisions, not individually attributable statements of Carlini’s preferences. The first-in-setting polynomial-time priority claim belongs to the authors and is not independently verified here. White-box mechanism checks must be distinguished from the intended label-only attack. The acknowledgment credits Isaac Canales-Martínez with experiments shaping findings, proofreading, and reviewing others’ code, without identifying specific changes or Carlini’s role; it is not independent replication. Adaptive sampling and an optimized third-party implementation are proposed rather than demonstrated.
tensions_and_counterevidence: Hard-label output restriction coexists with strong architecture, input-domain, and precision assumptions. Neurons invisible to decision-boundary geometry and singular linear systems can defeat recovery; calling such cases unlikely in normally trained networks is an author assessment. Heuristic sign voting and genericity assumptions qualify broad extraction guarantees. Numerical filters eliminate observed false positives, not all possible errors. Fixed minima are 100 successful trials for layers 1 and 4 and 1,000 for layers 2 and 3, although adaptive allocation might be cheaper. Six layer-2 and seven layer-3 neurons initially remain at no more than 75% confidence; fresh-data reruns improve confidence without establishing a calibrated sequential-testing protocol or uniformly near-certain decisions. Conditional parameter precision does not establish whole-network functional equivalence. The showcase’s size does not make its modest-accuracy dense architecture representative of modern high-performing vision systems.
coverage_notes: Many records repeat the same passages and should count as one project. The conclusion’s description of extracting approximately one million parameters must retain the perfect-prior-layer assumption, symbolic-gradient substitution, omitted clustering cost, and deferred end-to-end implementation. Component timings cannot simply be summed into a complete black-box attack cost. The supplied version contains only a placeholder software-release URL, so usable software availability is not established. Underlying Figure 10 measurements are not supplied beyond the reported precision summary. Algorithmic retry/discard rules are concrete procedure choices, not evidence of a general personal research-stopping philosophy.

substance:
The paper asks whether moving from bounded classifier attacks to general-purpose LLM security permits cumulative, measurable progress. Its method is a position argument organized around defining problems, constructing attacks and defenses, and evaluating results, drawing on cited studies rather than new experiments. Free-form helpfulness and harmfulness goals make success partly subjective; asking a model to repeat supplied harmful text need not expose a meaningful new vulnerability. Discrete inputs, weak proxy objectives, personas, and multi-turn social engineering help explain the cited advantage of human-designed attacks over automated optimization, which also weakens worst-case evaluation and adaptive training.

Evaluation criticisms are concrete: harmless non-refusals can be counted as jailbreaks; judges can themselves be attacked; and using the same judge inside a defense and its evaluation can produce perfect measured safety by construction. Refusing everything is safe but useless, so retained utility must also be assessed. Silent updates and undisclosed preprocessing or postprocessing obstruct stable comparisons. Criticism of the reviewed defenses concerns the absence of well-defined, analyzable security properties, not proof that they never protect users.

Application-specific distinctions matter. An 'unfinetunable' model cannot literally prevent weight edits; evaluation must ask whether edits produce useful new behavior while retaining utility and must search both inputs and much larger parameter spaces. Poisoning effects can be overwritten by subsequent training stages, requiring attention to the full training sequence, clean retraining baselines, and ablations that frontier-model costs impede. Prompt injection can have directly measurable outcomes, such as unauthorized email sending, while still requiring realistic tool scaffolding and difficult multi-turn attack search, sometimes without intermediate traces.

For membership inference, apparent knowledge of Harry Potter could come from reviews or Wikipedia rather than the original book. The evidentiary target is counterfactual: behavior should be unlikely without training on the particular sample. Overlapping corpora, post-hoc nonmember distribution shifts, and later training beyond advertised cutoffs complicate that inference. For unlearning, removing a datapoint differs from removing a concept: eliminating bioweapons knowledge while retaining biology and virology creates a specification–utility conflict. Failure to generate information does not prove erasure from weights; adaptive tests must also examine collateral capability changes and possible privacy leakage.

The principal recommendation separates two legitimate purposes. Practical vulnerability demonstrations can remain valuable on fuzzy problems when harm is clear and immediate. Work claiming scientific understanding should instead identify formal, scoped subproblems that support comparison and cumulative results. Formalization is proposed as enabling measurement, not guaranteeing that robustness becomes easy.
attribution_limits: These are collective arguments and recommendations by the coauthors, not individually attributable statements of Carlini's preferences or a documented personal reviewing procedure. The supplied material reports literature-based assessments, illustrative scenarios, and proposed evaluation standards; it does not report new longitudinal benchmarks, poisoning experiments, agent benchmarks, or unlearning measurements.
tensions_and_counterevidence: The provocative title is qualified: the authors acknowledge progress against average-case vulnerabilities and practical protection from system scaffolding while arguing that worst-case robustness has barely improved. They explicitly consider the alternative that increased difficulty reflects finally confronting realistic, unconstrained security rather than choosing the wrong problems. Patching systems can help users while harming reproducibility. Their concern about opaque scaffolding is not opposition to every system-level control. These qualifications are positions within the paper, not documented changes of mind.
coverage_notes: Numerous records repeat the same passages and must count as one position paper, not independent support. Some quotations contain extraction artifacts, including an incomplete phrase about a 'well-defined formal'; no missing formalism is reconstructed. The parameter-space comparison of roughly 1000-fold greater dimensionality is illustrative, not a universal measured constant.

substance:
This position paper examines public pretraining followed by differentially private fine-tuning along two independent dimensions: privacy and usefulness. It additionally separates model-output privacy from confidentiality during training and inference. The central scope correction is that private fine-tuning protects the fine-tuning dataset, not the preceding non-private corpus. Public accessibility does not establish nonsensitivity or informed consent: contact information posted for research correspondence, accidental disclosures, and information published by others can acquire much broader exposure through model-mediated redistribution. Consent would need to explain disclosure to downstream users, not merely participation in product improvement. Massive, weakly curated corpora make provenance and consent difficult, while broad 'privacy-preserving' labels could undermine trust in differential privacy even when the formal technique is not at fault.

The benchmark analysis distinguishes distributional overlap from duplicate records. ImageNet-to-CIFAR-10 transfer may largely adapt already learned object classes to lower resolution even if the datasets are disjoint. A particularly revealing terminology example calls proprietary JFT pretraining 'public' while downloadable ImageNet is the 'private' target; near-duplicate removal does not answer the distributional critique. Incomparable pretraining resources—from ImageNet and CIFAR-100 to an engineered single image—confound representation-learning gains with private-learning improvements. The cited CLIP zero-shot CIFAR-10 accuracy of 96.2% illustrates that high performance can require no access to the nominally private training set; this is an existing result, not a new experiment.

The authors frame transfer uncertainty through 'Transfermania,' where public representations cover sensitive tasks, and 'Privacyland,' where they do not. Resolving the question requires data resembling actual sensitive applications, with medical records, email, and reviews offered as examples. They explicitly decline to prescribe a benchmark because adequate justification requires a separate investigation, and recommend continuing work on DP learning without pretraining regardless of transfer's eventual success.

Deployment analysis uses a conditional minimum-accuracy scenario: a large DP model may protect training contributors but require inference users to upload sensitive inputs, whereas a smaller local model may meet accuracy only with weaker training-data protection. Oversized models can similarly force centralized training-data collection. Cryptographic computation and trusted execution are considered alternatives, but their feasibility is judged against the historical model and hardware setting. Task-specific distillation is proposed to enable smaller local models.

The broader agenda includes consent procedures, audits of open and proprietary datasets, datasheet disclosures, and data/model lifecycle evaluation covering collection, retention, and repeated training. DP pretraining also leaves an unresolved granularity question: sentence-level protection may inadequately cover sensitive information repeated across many sources.
attribution_limits: The substantive material is identified as the paper's first version. Its critiques, normative judgments, and research agenda are collaborative, not evidence of Carlini's private preferences or future project allocation. Numerical examples and motivating incidents come from cited or reported work. No new consent study, trust measurement, dataset audit, distillation result, or benchmark-design investigation is supplied. The informal description of DP should not replace its parameter- and privacy-unit-dependent formal guarantee.
tensions_and_counterevidence: The conclusion explicitly credits public-data research with demonstrating useful DP on complex problems without devastating utility loss. The authors allow that Transfermania may be real and would be encouraging; their skeptical alternative is not established empirically. Distribution overlap can be acceptable when measuring absolute performance on the particular task rather than generic learning progress. Remote deployment can be appropriate for nonsensitive inputs. The local-versus-remote tradeoff assumes that a small, strongly private model misses the required accuracy; it is not universal. Explaining two tiers of protection may still conflict with people's privacy expectations, so communication alone is not presented as a complete remedy.
coverage_notes: Repeated evidence records describe one conceptual project. Feasibility claims about model size, cryptography, and local execution belong to the supplied historical v1 text, not verified present-day limits. The paper's refusal to specify benchmarks is a local scope boundary, not a general personal stopping rule. Its critique does not invalidate the fine-tuning dataset's formal DP guarantee.

substance:
The project investigates why label-only attacks on standalone classifiers deteriorate when deployed preprocessing is included. The attacker submits valid 8-bit images, receives labels, and has limited queries; success means targeted or untargeted misclassification with small L2 perturbation in the original image space. Non-injective cropping, resizing, quantization, and compression can erase queried changes, wasting queries. Tuning and longer runs did not eliminate degradation in the tested settings; one motivating distortion comparison rises from 3.7 to 28.5.

The response combines extracting the preprocessing pipeline with adapted evasion. Bypassing runs an existing attack in processed space and then recovers an original-space image. For cropping, it attacks only retained pixels and restores untouched borders. For resizing, a Moore–Penrose pseudoinverse gives minimum-norm perturbation recovery for a fixed model-space adversarial target. Bypassing assumes idempotence and continuous outputs. When quantization or other conditions obstruct it, Biased-Gradient instead steers original-space queries toward changes that survive preprocessing, using differentiable versions of quantization and JPEG for gradient propagation. It can also be preferable when model-space distance poorly matches the original-space objective. Composed pipelines are bypassed and recovered in reverse order only when all stages permit it; otherwise the whole pipeline receives Biased-Gradient treatment.

Extraction is candidate-based guess-and-check, not unrestricted reconstruction. Two binary searches produce differently classified images differing at one pixel by 1/255, taking approximately 40 queries. Candidate-preserving pre-images then test whether the guessed transformation matches observed behavior. The implementation uses one unstable pair, with additional pairs available at greater cost. HuggingFace was selected because preprocessing metadata allowed verification; each experiment sampled ten ImageNet-1k models. Restricting a broad resizing search over dimensions 200–800 to typical pipelines reduced reported average extraction cost from 632 queries to roughly 50, conditional on candidate coverage.

Evaluation uses established Boundary Attack, Sign-OPT, HSJA, and QEBA implementations, sweeps hyperparameters for every attack, and ordinarily compares mean perturbation over 1,000 random samples at 5,000 queries each. For a 256-to-224 crop, unaware distances were 8–16% larger, close to an approximately 14% geometric prediction of wasted border perturbation. Extending QEBA budgets from 500 to 50,000 revealed a plateau near 10,000 without closing the awareness gap. Illustrated bypassing gains remained around 4.5–4.8-fold across budgets, whereas Biased-Gradient gains increased with more queries.

Tests also included neural preprocessors violating idempotence and two additional architecture/preprocessor pairings: EfficientNetV2-Tiny with resizing and DEIT3-Small with JPEG, showing approximately fourfold and twofold improvements. The authors recommend amortizing extraction and tuning across many attacks, while leaving optimal tuning-budget allocation unresolved.
attribution_limits: The methods, engineering choices, experiments, and recommendations are collective project evidence; no individual division of labor or personal preference is supplied. The pseudoinverse optimum concerns the specified real-valued linear recovery problem, not globally optimal adversarial search under all image constraints. Proposed matrix-construction and caching alternatives are not unambiguously identified as the implementation used in every experiment.
tensions_and_counterevidence: The broad claim that even the least efficient aware attack beats all unaware attacks has exceptions in individual small-input and high-quality-preprocessing settings. Best-of-sweep results do not fully budget an unknown attacker's tuning costs; equal five-setting sweeps do not ensure equally comprehensive searches. SwinIR GPU-memory limits forced 128-by-128 inputs, making raw distances incomparable with experiments at other resolutions. Success on non-idempotent neural preprocessors does not remove the formal assumption. The extraction test's 0.01 threshold depends on its detection-probability model, not a universal correctness guarantee. The two extra architectures vary preprocessing simultaneously, limiting causal generalization.
coverage_notes: Repeated records describe one project. Additional implementation details include an adapted SNS baseline, a pinned Foolbox commit, greedy integer-valued pre-image construction, and relaxed recovery using ten multiplier-search steps, reduced to three for expensive neural preprocessors. Resizing can use analytical or slower implementation-robust matrix construction, followed by per-input solving or cached pseudoinversion. Empirical QEBA sampling ratios shrink from 1/8 to 1/32 as original dimensions rise from 256 to 1024. A threshold-classifier toy explanation applies directly to nearest-neighbor resizing, not necessarily bilinear or bicubic interpolation.

substance:
This study asks whether models emit substantially copied training content despite defenses against verbatim reproduction, during malicious extraction and ordinary prompting alike. Because Copilot's corpus and filtering implementation were unavailable, the authors built MemFree as an inspectable analogue, not a reconstruction of Copilot. Whole-output rejection can leave a confident model repeatedly producing unacceptable text, so MemFree instead removes next-token probability when a token would complete a prohibited training n-gram, preserving novel portions of the generation.

Inference efficiency shaped the implementation: only the newly completed n-gram is checked, and a Bloom filter provides compact membership lookup while accepting false-positive suppression of novel text. Rather than expensive loss-screening of every training substring, experiments stored Pile ten-grams occurring at least ten times. The ten-token length was chosen through qualitative experience and storage considerations, balancing common-phrase suppression against missed shorter copies, not optimized against a clear objective. Bloom-filter absence of false negatives applies only to inserted entries.

Public training-data access determined the controlled model choice: four GPT-Neo sizes from 125M to 6B, using greedy decoding. Evaluation reused 30,000 training strings in thirty duplication-frequency buckets, with 50-token prompts and 50-token continuations. Approximate copying was measured through BLEU and normalized character-level Levenshtein similarity; a BLEU threshold around 0.75 came from qualitative inspection and audience interpretability. Applying this broader criterion to a prior prefix-extraction experiment increased detected memorization by up to twofold, conditional on the imperfect metric.

MemFree substantially reduced similarity and generally left already-dissimilar generations little changed. For the evaluated 6B model, more than 12,000 verbatim reproductions fell to four; all four involved strings omitted by the frequency cutoff. Nevertheless, near-copies remained, sometimes differing in only a few tokens, notably numerical lists. In 0.16% of samples, filtering increased similarity by more than 0.1. Pythia experiments, including original and deduplicated Pile variants, found more approximate memorization and somewhat weaker defense effectiveness.

Copilot's blocked Quake fast inverse square root continuation reappeared under Python-style comment formatting or renamed French variables. Ordinary prompts also bypassed filtering through small surface changes; unexpected whitespace behavior motivated a tabs-versus-spaces hypothesis. Separate GPT-3 and PaLM style tests used likely memorized public documents and fixed 100-word prompts and 50-word continuations, avoiding capitalization-induced token-count confounds without establishing training membership.

Utility analysis checked benchmark reference texts for blocked n-grams rather than measuring actual defended task scores, revealing potential interference with summarization and non-English text. The team restricted extraction demonstrations to extensively studied public datasets and shared the paper with GitHub and OpenAI before submission, while acknowledging that public availability does not eliminate privacy concerns.
attribution_limits: An explicit author-contribution statement credits Carlini with identifying weaknesses in memory-free decoding, working on MemFree implementation, running GPT-Neo experiments, and contributing to writing. It credits Ippolito with the original Bloom-filter defense idea, Tramèr with style-transfer prompting, and Nasr with Copilot experiments. These are reported contributions, not first-person testimony or sole authorship of every decision. Pythia experiments and disclosure communications are not individually assigned. GPT-3/PaLM tests concern transformed reproduction and hypothetical comparable filtering, not verified deployed filters.
tensions_and_counterevidence: The idealized 'perfect' defense and frequency-filtered implementation have different coverage. Memorization counts are not privacy-harm counts: the study does not distinguish private disclosure from acceptable quotation. The authors retain exact matching as an efficient test for obvious memorization and propose broader, domain-dependent definitions rather than abandoning it. Their own approximate metric can overcount and undercount. Main-text caution contrasts with stronger appendix confidence; a high-threshold claim about avoiding false negatives conflicts with its lower-bound rationale. Similarity increases have a proposed posterior-redirection explanation, not an isolated causal demonstration. Nominally same-size GPT-3 versions differ, but training composition and methods are not separately identified.
coverage_notes: Repeated records concern one project. Main text uses BLEU greater than 0.75, while the appendix says 0.75 or higher; the displayed edit-similarity formula also leaves a distance-versus-similarity ambiguity. Query instrumentation reports 49.8 ms for 10,000 lookups on one CPU core, mean 42.1 queries per generation, frequent first/tenth-token hits, and usually fewer than five alterations—not universal end-to-end latency. Source exemptions, longer n-grams, lower false-positive rates, and plagiarism-detection methods are proposals, not validated fixes. Appendix rendering loses color annotations and truncates its final examples.

substance:
The project studies a supply-chain backdoor whose objective is increased membership leakage from a victim's later fine-tuning dataset, rather than incorrect test-time predictions. The attacker modifies an existing clean checkpoint, preserves its architecture and useful performance, and then loses control: the victim trains on unpoisoned data with its own algorithm. The principal targeted setting assumes candidate records are already known and asks whether they were subsequently used, not how to reconstruct unknown records. Later access is black-box but includes confidence or log-probability information, rather than uniformly label-only or generated-text-only access.

For CLIP, poisoning maximizes loss on candidate targets while an auxiliary benign-data objective preserves ordinary capability. Subsequent fine-tuning should lower member losses more than nonmember losses, creating a stronger membership signal. This approach did not transfer comparably to language models, prompting an explicit reversal: minimize target loss to induce memorization first, then rely on reinforcement of included records and forgetting of excluded ones. Difficulty attaining sufficiently high language-model loss is offered as a tentative explanation, not an established mechanism.

Vision experiments use LiRA with sixteen shadow models, five random seeds, and ImageNet, CIFAR-10, and CIFAR-100, measuring accuracy before and after fine-tuning. Language experiments combine synthetic names, addresses, telephone numbers, and emails with ai4Privacy records and repeated canaries in WikiText-103. ClinicalBERT/MIMIC-IV experiments construct 150 fake-patient records involving rare diseases, selecting 75 as targets. These are controlled records, not recovered patient identities. Results emphasize TPR at 1% FPR, AUC, and task utility: one ai4Privacy comparison increases TPR from 0.049 to 0.874 with unchanged reported post-fine-tuning validation loss.

Because victim behavior is uncontrolled, ablations examine linear probing, LoRA, QLoRA, and Neftune, plus inference quantization, top-five log probabilities, and watermarking. Four-bit inference reduces leakage but raises validation loss from 3.19 to 3.58; poisoning still strengthens inference relative to its corresponding baseline. Non-target records also show increased leakage. Varying the poisoning coefficient exposes a tradeoff between preserved CLIP accuracy and attack strength.

The appendix preserves failed alternatives. A parameter-change method calibrated on sixteen ClinicalBERT fine-tunings found approximately 200 informative locations per run but no consistent overlap across eight runs; success required controlling token-masking randomness, contrary to the intended threat model. Knowledge-neuron amplification tested 128 targets, ten templates, and about 9,000 attacks without reliable success, despite occasional exposure increases. The paper therefore distinguishes limited demonstrations from practical backdoors under victim-controlled training. Its mitigation agenda calls for stronger checkpoint validation and trainer-provided checksums to hinder modified reuploads, without claiming checksums establish that an original model is benign.
attribution_limits: The attack design, objective reversal, experiments, negative results, and mitigation recommendations are collective work; the packet supplies no individual contribution allocation or first-person preference statement by Carlini. The impact statement identifies public awareness and better validation as the authors' purpose, but does not document a particular disclosure exchange. Controlled canary insertion and repetition do not establish naturally occurring leakage rates or compromise of an actual victim deployment.
tensions_and_counterevidence: The threat model is weaker specifically in fine-tuning-data and training-control requirements, but still requires adoption of attacker-modified weights and, for the principal attack, known candidate records. Unchanged architecture and retained accuracy operationalize stealth without proving resistance to dedicated detection. QLoRA substantially weakens leakage; its prose claims a validation-loss decrease while the table indicates higher loss than corresponding LoRA settings. Non-target spillover is qualitatively supported, but inconsistent percentage/proportion notation prevents safely repeating its exact rates. Black-box effectiveness with top-five probabilities does not establish effectiveness with text-only access.
coverage_notes: Repeated evidence records describe one project. The appendix does not establish the chronological order of unsuccessful alternatives. Knowledge-neuron exploration used a coarse-to-fine search yielding roughly five to ten neurons, activation multipliers from one to twenty through connected weights, and target repetitions from one to one hundred; its negative conclusion is specific to those interventions. Checksums mitigate altered reuploads relative to a trusted release, not malicious original releases or every model-supply-chain threat.

substance:
The project asks whether components surrounding a predictor leak substantially more training- or query-data information than an equally capable attacker obtains from the standalone model. It covers training filters, preprocessing, output filters, and query filtering, using black-box model access, generally known surrounding components, and attack-specific poisoning or known-prefix capabilities. Training-filter experiments isolate one filter; public-data demonstrations are the authors' harm-reduction choice.

Deduplication turns target membership into absence of injected mislabeled duplicates. Approximate poisons resemble the target but not one another; constructed embeddings are inverted with 1,000 projected-gradient steps, and a checkerboard feature strengthens memorization in ablations. LiRA-style shadow-model confidence distributions support inference. Experiments use 250 random CIFAR-10 targets, 1–8 poisons, imagededup defaults, and ordinary versus poisoning-aware baselines. Classification attacks assume label-independent deduplication, mislabeled insertion, and training on all retained records; experiments sample half of CIFAR-10 and train for 100 epochs. Exact delete-all deduplication reaches 98% TPR at 0.01% FPR. Under unknown deduplication, the paper recommends one exact duplicate; the specialized multi-poison alternative requires confidence in approximate delete-all-but-one filtering and its threshold.

Investigations explicitly credited to Carlini include recovering tokenization from context-window truncation: a padded “favorite color is red” probe reveals token lengths. Recursive byte-pair concatenation recovers GPT-2's vocabulary in 819,869,857 queries; targeted recovery on enwiki8 costs approximately 30,000 queries per megabyte. Memorization-filter tests compare matching unfiltered completions against filtered ones, declaring absent baselines inconclusive. Permanent-filter tests repeat target strings to reduce ordinary completion uncertainty. A hypothetical GPT-Neo deployment inserts 1,000 synthetic OpenSSH keys into a 20-token Bloom filter, rather than demonstrating underlying model memorization. Above-99.9% next-token accuracy remains insufficient across over 10,000 Base64 candidates; depth-first search prioritized using frequencies from 10 TB of random data recovers about 90% of keys, averaging 338,000–376,000 queries. Copilot's undocumented, apparently approximate filter yields a likely October 2021 cutoff from frequent tqdm commits, not a verified internal date.

Other experiments expose composition failures: FoolsGold participation inference achieves 85% versus a strong 67.5% baseline using similarly distributed, nonoverlapping attacker records over ten runs. With 256 approximate duplicates, initially neighboring datasets diverge after deduplication; 128 DP-SGD runs yield end-to-end epsilon lower bounds 7.5/17/22 against nominal training budgets 1/1.5/3. This concerns preprocessing sensitivity, not invalid DP mathematics. A global evasion detector reveals prior query membership with 100% TPR and 0% FPR on 1,000 queried versus 1,000 held-out images.
attribution_limits: Collective contribution statements credit Carlini and Florian Tramèr with the central problem; Carlini with proposing vocabulary extraction; Carlini and Eric Wallace with proposing memorization-filter leakage; and Carlini with corresponding experiments and drafting. They separately credit Tramèr with the deduplication idea, Edoardo Debenedetti with deduplication and query-filter experiments, Giorgio Severi and Matthew Jagielski with poisoning experiments, and Milad Nasr with Copilot and DP-SGD experiments. These are explicit role assignments, not personal preference statements or evidence that Carlini individually selected every implementation detail. Technical interpretations and recommendations remain collaborative.
tensions_and_counterevidence: Despite finding adversarial leakage, the authors recommend continuing deduplication because they judge duplicated-data privacy risks worse. They also identify the same side channel in a poisoning defense previously proposed by Carlini, without documenting his personal reaction or a change of mind. Specialized deduplication attacks fail under the wrong filtering variant or when the real threshold falls outside the stated interval between the squared guess and the guess. Survival under ±2% threshold errors does not establish that every randomized-threshold defense fails. Activation clustering reaches only 70% membership precision because benign records contaminate target clusters; its mechanism description inconsistently states which cluster sizes are removed. Copilot inference permits false positives. The assertion that public-data demonstrations pose no real-world privacy risk is the authors' assessment, not an independently established fact.
coverage_notes: Many records repeat identical quotations and contribution credits; they describe one project, not independent corroboration. The text attribute-inference extension assumes a known template and low-arity, simplified one-token unknown attribute and supplies a construction rather than numerical evaluation. Leakage from model-extraction detectors is conditional on adopting global query logs, not a tested deployment. Composition-aware differential privacy and randomized query-filter thresholds are proposed future work. Attacks equally applicable to isolated models, and attacks on ML-based caches or databases, are outside the stated scope. The reported perfect and near-perfect results remain specific to their experimental conditions.

substance:
This study uses formal verification to distinguish genuine robustness from failure of available attacks. Its reference quantity is the minimum distortion required for a targeted adversarial example, certified for a particular network, input, metric, and numerical precision. The authors acknowledge that L-infinity and L1 are imperfect perceptual metrics but retain them for comparability with prior work.

Verification tractability determines the experimental scale: a three-layer fully connected MNIST network has fewer than 100 hidden neurons, 24 per layer, approximately 20,000 weights, and 97% accuracy. Reluplex checks whether adversarial examples exist within candidate distortion bounds. Binary search stops when the upper–lower interval is below 0.001. A CW-generated adversarial example supplies a tight initial upper bound to reduce expensive solver calls. L1 distances are encoded through absolute-value expressions using ReLUs without changing solver code, adding 784 constraints and worsening computational performance.

The evaluation crosses ordinary and adversarially trained networks, both metrics, ten arbitrarily selected test images, and all nine incorrect target labels: 90 searches per network–metric condition. Completed searches are separated from timeouts; a timeout contributes only the smallest adversarial upper bound found, not a completed optimality certificate. Only six ordinary-network L1 searches finish, so that condition is excluded from substantive attack-quality conclusions and the defense comparison. The latter uses 35 matched L-infinity instances completed on both networks.

On those matched instances, mean minimum distortion increases from 0.039 to 0.165 under adversarial training, approximately 4.2-fold. This is positive evidence of actual robustness improvement within the verified threat model rather than merely obscuring an attack. However, seven of the 35 source–target instances become less robust, averaging 12.8% degradation. Verified examples improve on CW by approximately 12% on both ordinary and hardened networks, providing no evidence of attack-specific overfitting in this test.

The certified solutions also diagnose optimization failures. Some require 30–40% less distortion than iterative attacks; a hardened-network digit 9 shows improvements of 21–47% across targets. Taking a small step toward the known optimum enables gradient descent to find it, whereas random steps offer little help. This uses otherwise unavailable solution knowledge and is diagnostic, not a deployable improvement. Hardened networks unexpectedly verify more readily: 81 versus 38 completed L-infinity searches and 64 versus six L1 searches. Counting ReLU activation-region switches finds no statistically significant difference, leaving the proposed reduced-nonlinearity explanation unsupported and the solver phenomenon unresolved.
attribution_limits: The supplied material reports decisions, experiments, and interpretations in the collective voice of Carlini, Guy Katz, Clark Barrett, and David Dill. It supplies no contribution breakdown establishing who chose the metrics, implemented the encoding, or performed the diagnostic interventions. Carlini's listed first authorship does not establish individual ownership of those choices or private preferences. The numerical results are reported research findings, not independent validation.
tensions_and_counterevidence: The favorable average defense result coexists with seven verified degradations, large individual CW optimality gaps, extensive solver timeouts, and completion-based selection. The source's wording of a 423% improvement is misleading under the usual percentage-increase convention: 0.165/0.039 is approximately 4.23-fold, or a 323% increase. The nonlinearity check only tests the chosen activation-switch measure. Neither absence of observed attack-specific overfitting nor successful small-network verification establishes security at larger scale, under other metrics, or across all inputs.
coverage_notes: Repeated evidence records are duplicate descriptions of one study. The ten source images were arbitrarily selected, not established as representative; the 35 matched cases are source–target instances rather than 35 independent source images. The tractability limit describes the tools available for this work, not a timeless verification ceiling. The paper proposes releasing minimum-distortion examples for future evaluation, but the supplied evidence does not establish that release occurred. Selecting representative evaluation points remains an open question.

substance:
The question is incremental deployment risk: does publishing an efficient model give attackers additional leverage against its server counterpart? The objective is not complete adversarial robustness, but avoiding added harm while fixing server training, preserving server/on-device accuracy, and minimizing construction cost. Fully independent training is a conceptual solution rejected as operationally duplicative; the experimental independently trained baseline is narrower, using the same architecture.

Across 19 model pairs, six construction mechanisms, CIFAR10 and ImageNet, attackers receive white-box device access but limited server queries. Only server queries count as cost; transfer's “zero cost” excludes local computation. Success probability is primary, with query cost supplementary and relative fooling rate normalizing transferred accuracy loss against a white-box reference. FGSM, PGD-10, and P-RGF use the same 1,000 random test examples, 8/255 L-infinity perturbations, 2/255 steps, five repetitions, and a 4,000-query failure cutoff.

Quantized/pruned priors reduce query costs by roughly two orders of magnitude in strong CIFAR10 cases. Tested SageMaker Edge models are functionally identical to server counterparts, enabling approximately 100% success below 20 queries. AutoML instead requires an assumed reverse-engineered surrogate; its adapted optimization attack fails, with integer-image rounding offered as an explanation. Distillation increases vulnerability for ResNet18 but not NASNet. Ordinary 200-epoch fine-tuning reduces FGSM transfer but leaves PGD-10 RFR near 1 and query success unchanged.

Defense design compares logits, activations, and input-gradient cosine similarities, choosing gradients as the best empirical predictor. Twenty-epoch similarity-unpairing combines classification loss with a dissimilarity penalty. Activation penalties fail; an effective gradient setting preserves accuracy and reduces query fooling to 15%. Combining output and gradient penalties adds only about 0.02 transfer-RFR improvement, so subsequent experiments use one penalty.

Integration is conditional on construction: before, after, or jointly with compression. Post-quantization fine-tuning preserves 91% CIFAR10 accuracy, versus 68% before quantization; joint quantization reaches only 47%, so vulnerability evaluation stops. Joint pruning's dropout-mask implementation reaches 20% accuracy, while pre-pruning unpairing limits tolerable sparsity to 30–40%. Joint distillation excludes output dissimilarity because it opposes teacher-student matching. Compact-architecture joint training loses 20–30% accuracy, prompting detailed reporting only of post-training fine-tuning. Once-for-all post-fine-tuning raises query cost from 28 to 220 but only reduces success from 100% to 97%, with PGD-10 RFR 0.98. ImageNet follow-up improves gradually yet leaves PGD-10 RFR near 0.9. These outcomes distinguish increased attack effort from preventing successful attacks.
attribution_limits: These are collective project choices and reported findings by Sanghyun Hong, Carlini, and Alexey Kurakin; no supplied contribution statement assigns individual decisions. Preserving accuracy, avoiding retraining, and giving attackers substantial capability are explicit project-level priorities, not Carlini's independently stated personal preferences. Commercial-service observations concern configurations tested at the time. Reverse engineering in the AutoML attack is an assumption, and proposed extensions are not demonstrated capabilities.
tensions_and_counterevidence: Accuracy preservation is a goal, not a universal outcome: large penalty weights can damage accuracy; from-scratch output/feature penalties lose 7–15%, although combined penalties can match the best fine-tuning result. Increasing the output penalty can cost another 2–3%. MobileNetV2 benefits more than SqueezeNet, whose query-attack metrics can worsen. The distillation narrative claims strong joint-training results, but Table VIII instead shows increased PGD-10 relative fooling rate and query success for both students; this cannot support unqualified success. Robust server training improves query resistance at a reported 10–20% accuracy cost while retaining high relative transfer vulnerability; weak query attacks remain a competing explanation. Robust distillation offers comparable protection with accuracy loss, and a RobNet check still finds useful quantized/pruned attack priors. Stronger attacks, repeated releases, and whether the cost-security trade-off is inherent remain unresolved. The recommendation to condition releases on security mitigation is broader than the evaluated cases.
coverage_notes: Repeated records describe one project. Image classification was selected for tractability and mature attacks; text classification, extraction, and inversion are motivations or suggested extensions, not evaluated results. Initial pruning increases sparsity by 5% until accuracy loss exceeds 4%, producing roughly 50% sparsity. Architecture comparisons use shared-weight once-for-all subnetworks and an explicitly imperfect configuration-distance proxy. Progressive-shrinking joint optimization was judged intractable. Supplied evidence flags inconsistent similarity-sample descriptions, query-versus-success wording in the vulnerability definition, an AutoML FGSM numerical inconsistency, and an applicability table contradicted by later OFA restrictions. Activation cosine similarity also has permutation and dimensionality limitations. Five-run language is qualified by use of a single supplied pretrained OFA model.

substance:
The study moves from demonstrating that extraction exists to quantifying extractable training text and its relationship to model size, duplication, and prompt length. It deliberately supplies known training prefixes to maximize discoverability, a stronger information setting than practical attackers necessarily possess. Its operational definition uses greedy decoding and exact reproduction of a 50-token continuation; counterfactual and differential-privacy-based alternatives are set aside because hundreds or thousands of training runs are impractical at this scale.

Rather than exhaustively evaluate an approximately 800 GB corpus at an estimated cost exceeding 30 GPU-years, the researchers use roughly 50,000-sequence subsets. Uniform sampling estimates absolute prevalence; duplication- and length-normalized sampling studies rare high-repetition, long-context conditions. A suffix array makes frequency-bucket sampling feasible through linear scans. Absolute rates from the biased sample are explicitly not corpus-wide prevalence estimates.

Larger models generally reproduce more training text, and repetition increases extraction, but context affects discoverability without changing the model. In the biased sample, the 6B model's extraction rises from 33% with 50 context tokens to 65% with 450. Varying total sequence length separately while holding model and repetition fixed produces nearly overlapping curves, supporting a context-length rather than intrinsic document-length explanation. GPT-2, trained on WebText rather than The Pile, supplies a control for generic prediction ability, although corpus overlap prevents treating it as certainly unexposed.

A 100-beam sensitivity check increases extraction by under two percentage points on average, at most 5.6%. Random decoding is omitted because novelty conflicts with the study's discovery objective, not because its inferiority is universally proved. Searching the whole corpus for generated continuations finds substantially more memorization: at 100 repetitions, 32.6% versus 15.8% under expected-suffix matching. The cheaper single-suffix test is nevertheless retained for computational feasibility and reproducibility, knowingly yielding a looser lower bound.

Replication revises the expectation that all trends generalize cleanly: model-size effects transfer more consistently than duplication effects. T5 requires exact masked-token reconstruction rather than continuation; one mask per sequence is used across 50,000 sequences. A statistically significant nonmonotonic repetition result prompts inspection, revealing whitespace-heavy examples in the 138–158 repetition bucket. Deduplicated C4 models show roughly threefold improvement below 35 original repetitions and benefits up to approximately 100, but not above that range; imperfect deduplication is a hypothesis, not an established sole cause. OPT's lower extraction on Pile-derived prompts remains ambiguous between better curation and training-distribution mismatch because its original corpus is unavailable.
attribution_limits: The source explicitly states alphabetical author ordering, so Carlini's first position does not establish leadership or individual ownership. Definitions, sampling choices, findings, and revised expectations are collective. The preference for an actionable extractability definition is task-specific, not a personal rejection of counterfactual memorization. Adequacy of one T5 mask per sequence is the authors' assessment, not a separately demonstrated mask-sensitivity result. Reported extractability is a measurement under favorable prompting, not demonstrated extraction by an attacker lacking training data.
tensions_and_counterevidence: Deduplication helps but does not eliminate leakage, including at low repetition counts. Larger models' memorized sets are not supersets: even the 125M model reproduces some sequences the 6B model does not. One illustrative case has the small model copying a formatting-induced typo while larger models try to correct it, exposing an exact-match limitation rather than reversing the aggregate size trend. Hard-to-discover memorization can impede attackers and conceal failures from auditors. The paper's prompt-length restriction recommendation is explicitly conditional on stronger attacks not yet being available, not a current or complete guarantee. Lower OPT extraction cannot be equated with lower intrinsic memorization, and T5's changed task prevents straightforward comparison of absolute rates with causal models.
coverage_notes: Repeated quotations are dependent evidence from one project. Roughly 50,000-sequence subsets and the approximately 500,000-sequence normalized collection across lengths describe different aggregation levels, not interchangeable sample totals. Duplication counts in deduplicated-model comparisons refer to the original corpus, not necessarily retained training occurrences. Qualitative examples were randomly sampled within specified criteria and then selected for interest; they are illustrative rather than unbiased prevalence evidence. Exact matching omits approximate or semantically equivalent reproduction and valid alternative training continuations. The reported revision concerns this collaboration's experimental expectations, not a documented personal change of worldview.

substance:
This project asked whether direct remote-model queries could elicit specified harmful strings and evade moderation without relying on transferability or a suitable transfer surrogate. GCQ decomposed GCG into gradient-dependent candidate filtering and query-only selection: a proxy proposed candidates, while the target determined quality. A best-first buffer of unexplored suffixes enabled early rejection when partial loss exceeded the worst retained candidate, reducing reported cost approximately 30%. Fixed iterations returned the best candidate. Optimization minimized negative cumulative target log probability, but success required actual greedy generation.

Implementation replaced uniform-random initialization with repeated target text, left-truncated to fit; initialization alone solved approximately 28% with 20-token prompts. Against 574 GPT-3.5 Turbo Instruct targets, the team used unaligned Mistral 7B as proxy, imposed $1 per target, and reported $80 aggregate cost. Success reached 79.6% within $0.10 and 86.0% within $0.20 per target. Targets no longer than 20 tokens reached 97.9%. All 39 failed longer targets succeeded after increasing prompts to 40 tokens and budgets to $2, averaging $0.41, although these simultaneous changes confound causal attribution. Random initialization succeeded on only two of the first 20 targets, supporting initialization dependence specifically under low-cost conditions. Adapted default AutoDAN GA/HGA configurations succeeded on 1/574 and 0/574, distinguishing exact-string generation from general jailbreaking.

A proxy-free variant first probed every position, then concentrated replacements where loss improved most. On Vicuna 7B it reportedly outperformed original GCG by about 30%; the optimized gradient-using variant was approximately twice as query-efficient. Retokenization prevented exploiting token sequences unreproducible as ordinary strings.

For moderation, suffix optimization minimized summed category scores without needing unpublished thresholds; success meant no flags. Already 197/574 strings were unflagged. Free, rate-limited OpenAI requests used batches of 32. Universal suffixes trained on 20 shuffled strings and evaluated on 554 held-out strings: 20-token suffixes reached 99.2% after 2,000 requests, versus 94.8% for five tokens after 40,000. At 320 queries, nonuniversal Llama Guard success was 59%/87% for five-/20-token suffixes versus OpenAI’s 84%/91%; the gap narrowed with additional queries.

After 1,000 measurements each on fixed generation and moderation inputs, the team judged loss noise small enough to leave unmitigated. A single solution recheck reproduced 519 targets, approximately 90%, which they accepted while deferring improvement.
attribution_limits: All methods, findings, judgments, and recommendations are collaborative work, not independently attributable decisions or preferences of Carlini. Algorithmic iteration limits and spending caps are not personal research-stopping rules. Rates, costs, API capabilities, and model behavior are historical reported measurements. Explanations involving weakened initialization versus insufficient prompt degrees of freedom remain hypotheses. Proposed perplexity-filter evasion and attacks without arbitrary-token probability estimation were not demonstrated.
tensions_and_counterevidence: The demonstrated generation attack requires estimating arbitrary-token log probabilities, despite being query-based and potentially proxy-free. Removal of prompt-token probabilities prompted a more expensive reconstruction method; parent-based bias estimates reportedly worked over 99% of the time, with binary-search fallback. A March 2024 API change made that reconstruction technique obsolete, and the paper described a more expensive alternative. The authors acknowledged that perplexity filtering could detect their random-looking strings. Nondeterminism persisted with fixed seeds and temperature zero, with unknown cause; fixed-input noise measurements and one recheck per solution do not establish long-run reliability. Long-target reruns changed both budget and prompt length. Strong initialization dependence led the authors to characterize NLP attack optimization as comparatively weak despite high success. Their defensive conclusion concerns defenses relying exclusively on breaking transferability, not the failure of all defenses.
coverage_notes: Repeated evidence entries describe one project and are not independent corroboration. Open-model experiments used batch size 512 and 500 iterations, permitting nearly 400 times the closed-model query allowance; cross-setting rates are not equal-budget comparisons. Moderation success includes already-unflagged strings, and held-out generalization is within the same dataset. One figure sublabel says 10 tokens while surrounding prose describes five versus 20. The February listing date does not encompass all supplied text, which also discusses March 2024 changes.

substance:
The paper investigates whether randomness itself explains the empirical robustness of randomized defenses, or whether aggregation and refinement retain that robustness without fresh random draws. Its motivating distinction is between genuinely reducing vulnerability and merely making a particular attack fail to locate existing adversarial examples. Low attack success alone cannot resolve that distinction.

The Nag Factor experiment adopts a deployment-specific objective: an attacker wins after any one misclassification, repeated queries are cheap and low-risk, and the same input can be resubmitted without optimization. Only hard-label feedback is required. Deterministic Smoothing resets the seed before every prediction, preserving corruption and aggregation but reusing the same corruptions. On CIFAR-10, the authors classified 100,000 Gaussian-corrupted copies per test datapoint, then shuffled and grouped predictions to estimate error probabilities across aggregation sizes and repeated-query budgets.

White-box comparisons reused each defense’s published implementation and original PGD variant. Randomized and deterministic smoothing converged in measured robust accuracy around five corruptions, versus the original setting of 100. The authors attributed this to self-ensembling nearby predictions. EBM–Def comparisons used one, two, or five refinement chains across four perturbation thresholds; near-identical behavior supported their interpretation that refinement, rather than random initialization, produced the measured benefit.

DiffPure materially qualified the broad thesis. A single fixed seed achieved 67% robust accuracy versus 88% for the randomized version; two alternating noise patterns achieved 83%, and three matched 88%. Experiments also considered cycles of five, ten, 50, and 100 seeds. A predictable multi-seed schedule is not an input-only classifier returning an invariant answer on repeated inputs.

For evaluation diagnostics, Subspace Grid-sweep searches constrained one- to six-dimensional orthonormal slices because full-space enumeration is infeasible. Equal-sized random sampling supplements the grid’s geometric blind spots, and PGD searches the same subspaces with one, ten, or twenty restarts. The case study contrasts an undefended model with k-Winners-Take-All, already known to obscure gradients. Against the union of vulnerabilities discovered by all methods, grid search recovered 0.95 and twenty-restart PGD 0.91 on the defended model; corresponding undefended figures were 0.98 and 1.00. These discrepancies suggest attack-search failure, not exhaustive vulnerability measurement.

The authors recommend avoiding randomness where possible and evaluating deterministic analogs when retaining it. They explicitly acknowledge lost smoothing certificates and propose investigating how knowledge of fixed seeds changes attacker capability, rather than treating the theory–experiment mismatch as resolved.
attribution_limits: These are coauthored experiments, interpretations, and recommendations, not explicit personal preferences or individually assigned contributions. Statements about prior defenses’ motivations must remain distinct from this paper’s position. The fixed-seed knowledge investigation and proposed black-box evaluations of deterministic analogs are future work. Reported attack performance establishes empirical findings for the tested implementations, not universal causal results about randomization.
tensions_and_counterevidence: Strictly fixed-seed DiffPure did not preserve all measured robustness; recovery with three seeds cannot be restated as equality for a single fixed corruption. Fixing smoothing draws removes the original Monte Carlo basis for certification, even if tested attacks perform similarly. An attacker knowing the fixed draws should in principle have an easier optimization problem, an unresolved discrepancy here. Randomness can genuinely hinder some black-box attacks and enable certification, while also burdening evaluators by obscuring loss surfaces and requiring tailored attacks. Repetition risk depends on application incentives and query controls. Grid and random search remain incomplete; their discovered union excludes vulnerabilities missed by every method.
coverage_notes: Numerous records repeat the same interventions and recommendations and count as one project. The diagnostic demonstration uses one previously identified gradient-obfuscation case rather than broad validation on unknown defenses. Original-code consistency controls implementation differences but does not establish that the chosen PGD attacks exhaust adaptive possibilities. The paper’s empirical argument principally concerns the studied white-box evaluations.

Carlini’s recreational objective was to read a roughly forty-year-old Apple ProFile drive without a working Lisa, not to recover information he actually needed. He says the drive was reportedly probably factory fresh and describes the project as undertaken for fun. The account follows two separate problems: restoring operation and implementing communication with the controller.

With no voltage on the expected five-volt rail, he hypothesized age-related capacitor failure and replaced all power-supply capacitors to reduce the risk of further damage. Expected five- and twelve-volt readings returned, but the disk still did not spin. He then distinguished a dead motor from a stuck mechanism, opened the drive, manually rotated it, repeated the intervention after hearing attempted movement, and warmed it under a heat lamp. The drive eventually spun, but he explicitly did not know which intervention fixed it. His interpretation of the self-test light also remained uncertain. He disclaimed hardware-repair expertise and warned that the post was not an instruction manual.

For data access, he used online manuals describing Apple’s proprietary Lisa-facing protocol over a standard DB-25 cable, translating its handshake into Arduino code step by step. Implementation accounted for inverted PSTRB, CMD, and BSY signals, while RRW remained uninverted. He bought an oscilloscope for the project and displayed four control channels, explicitly acknowledging that the traces did not simultaneously substantiate the data lines. Reproducible noise on BSY just before it went low convinced him the effect was probably real, but an explanation involving internal power draw remained speculation.

He accepted reading at roughly one-twentieth of the stated one-megahertz capability for 532-byte transfers because it was sufficient to image the disk. Reading every sector produced a five-megabyte image; meaningful strings and a byte-level visualization supported apparent success. Mounting the filesystem and interpreting its contents were deferred, so this was not verified complete semantic recovery.

Scope boundaries were explicit: he did not investigate the internal drive-to-controller parallel-port standard because the task did not require it, and he allotted under two hours to the write-up. He published reusable code but restricted safety assurances to his own successful experience, making no promise for other hardware. Enjoyment, sufficient functionality, and bounded explanation—not exhaustive diagnosis or maximum transfer speed—were the stated project priorities.

Capacitor failure and power-draw explanations are hypotheses, not established component-level diagnoses. Reported factory freshness is information he was told. The code’s operation and safety beyond his drive, image integrity, and filesystem recovery were not independently verified in the supplied material.
tensions_and_counterevidence: Successful operation did not yield causal certainty: manual rotation and warming were combined, and the self-test indicator was only tentatively interpreted. Control traces provided partial visibility, while readable strings were plausibility checks rather than byte-for-byte validation. He deliberately left some questions unanswered and stopped optimizing before reaching available bandwidth. These are task-specific limits in a hobby project, not evidence that his professional research uniformly accepts the same stopping criteria.
coverage_notes: Duplicate excerpts describe one recovery project. The unexamined internal interface must not be confused with the documented Lisa-facing protocol he implemented. The two-hour limit applies to writing, not the duration of the entire project. Carlini presents Regex Chess as holiday exploration undertaken with “entirely no purpose”: an ordered sequence of 84,688 regular expressions that produces a valid, reasonably competent chess move. His explicit broader preference is for low-pressure projects that are enjoyable and teach computer science outside one’s usual field, not a claim that professional research should abandon practical goals.

He first built a branch-free, conditionally executed SIMD-style virtual instruction set, then programmed chess on that substrate. Stack contents and variables occupy one string. Conditional execution changes an active-state marker so subsequent instructions stop matching, then reactivates the state later. Global substitutions operate across forked state blocks, a feature he calls his favorite. These are logical parallel states, not demonstrated hardware-parallel threads. The fixed instruction sequence cannot loop generally and is explicitly not Turing complete; bounded chess computations are implemented by unrolling loops.

Rather than build conventional parsing and code-generation stages, he used symbolic execution to record operations from Python-like programs, describing the result as closer to a macro-assembler than the compiler he had not intended to build. Repeated tracing directs conditionals toward less-visited branches before merging paths. Actual board processing expands FEN into 64 square variables; simplified FEN-like walkthroughs are disclosed as explanatory rather than literal implementation.

Move validation reuses legal-successor generation: apply the human’s proposed move, generate legal boards, and discard nonmatching states. Opponent replies already generated for king-safety checks are scored to obtain approximate two-ply minimax. He deliberately avoids the additional third-ply work needed by this implementation to validate every hypothetical opponent reply. Consequently, illegal opponent possibilities can make good moves look worse, although he states the engine’s actual moves remain legal.

Despite the recreational framing, he reports 2,000 lines of tests across several thousand games, with details such as castling and en passant omitted from the walkthrough. Performance work reduced approximately thirty minutes per reply to one–ten seconds on his machine. Dead-variable deletion and name reuse reduced reported internal state from 10 GB to about 300 MB, addressing linear scans and state copying. A preceding newline reportedly doubled one cleanup instruction’s efficiency. A slow piece-discovery loop justified replacing composed conditionals and stack operations with a specialized regex instruction. Candidate boards were also scored together because operations such as counting piece values apply identically across states.

The project therefore combined reusable abstractions with selective specialization, deliberate search approximation, and substantial reported testing. He bounded the explanation by referring readers to source code rather than walking through every piece.
attribution_limits: Architecture, implementation choices, enjoyment, favorite feature, and scope limits are explicitly Carlini’s account. Test volume, legality guarantees, timing improvements, and memory figures are self-reported; the supplied material contains neither executed tests nor independent benchmarks. The tracing strategy has no supplied general completeness proof or precise termination criterion. The linked source contains details not available here.
tensions_and_counterevidence: The title’s two-ply minimax description is qualified by unvalidated hypothetical opponent replies; this is an intentional playing-strength compromise, not fully legal two-ply minimax. Purposeless framing coexists with extensive reported tests and optimization for browser usability. Performance figures are position- and machine-dependent. The newline result concerns one instruction, not a twofold engine-wide speedup; its accompanying prose mentions a prefix absent from the displayed patterns, weakening the full causal explanation. Logical SIMD should not be inflated into multicore execution.
coverage_notes: Repeated excerpts concern one recreational project. Several walkthroughs are intentionally simplified pseudocode, and the engine’s real 64-variable board representation differs from the displayed examples. Omitted implementations, test coverage, and source-code behavior should not be reconstructed from their mention. This is direct evidence of exploratory interests and specific engineering decisions, not a universal professional research strategy.

The paper applies established timing-analysis techniques to a new domain: input-dependent inference acceleration can leak conversation information through encrypted traffic. It distinguishes passive production-service inference from secret recovery requiring active, repeated access to a fixed hidden prompt. The main adversary has cost-limited black-box access; gradients are investigated separately.

Controlled deployments wrapped FastChat in Nginx HTTPS on a separate cloud machine. A/B evaluation used 150-token outputs; easy/hard production checks measured the first 100 tokens, contrasting counting with primality code. Separate 500-query training and test sets gave GPT-3.5 94.7% accuracy, with over half the evaluated interactions identifiable at perfect precision. Token-level traces changed qualitatively around token 50 without revealing provider internals. To move beyond exact known messages, disjoint medical-advice/coding conversations extended to eight simulated rounds, excluding auxiliary ChatGPT-generated user replies from timing analysis.

Claude initially yielded only 60% success and precision-recall AUC below 0.7. Debugging identified multiple tokens per TCP packet; Gaussian packet-size buckets reconstructed token alignment, producing 100% A/B accuracy and AUC 1.0 using both size and timing. Month-long tests found Claude signatures effective throughout observation, GPT-3.5 eventually near chance, and GPT-4 gradually deteriorating.

The ChatGPT website required separate Selenium instrumentation. After GMM success below 30%, two convolutional layers plus a fully connected network classified timing/size traces. Using the first 400 packets and excluding shorter responses controlled total packet count. Single-message topic accuracies were 79%/82% for GPT-4/GPT-4o; ten-language top-1 accuracies were 49%/48%. Multi-turn website evaluation was deferred because instrumentation was difficult.

Active experiments aggregated modifier-specific classifiers across 1,000 Alpaca candidates and 100 modifiers, then pursued hidden numbers from 1–1,000. Speculative decoding supplied a mechanism: second-token latency signals rejection of the first draft token. GPT-4o paraphrase search replaced a weak manual question, improving discrimination from 56.2% to 97.2%; a larger target/draft pairing reached 99.3%. Ten iterations retained ten candidates each, reporting 910 suffixes scored on 1,000 numbers, 91 GPT-4o calls costing about $0.20, and under an A100-hour. Difficult phrasing exploited a capability gap: the draft answered no while the target usually answered correctly.

Constant-rate transmission addressed the timing channel through dummy messages and buffering. Ten-millisecond intervals added essentially no latency but 50–300% bandwidth; 80-millisecond intervals kept bandwidth overhead below 10% while adding 4–13 milliseconds per token. Protocol morphing was rejected on implementation/cost grounds, not through a new comprehensive comparison.
attribution_limits: This is joint work by Carlini and Nasr; problem selection, experiments, judgments, and disclosure cannot be assigned individually. The paper reports disclosure to OpenAI in January 2024 and Anthropic in April 2024, without provider responses or remediation details. Production measurements are historical. Applying familiar security techniques to efficient inference is the paper’s stated contribution, not an individual general preference about novelty. Proposed composition of imperfect digit inference with restricted-candidate recovery lacks a separate end-to-end result for arbitrary realistic secrets.
tensions_and_counterevidence: White-box optimization was a substantive negative result: replacing nondifferentiable runtime with a target-versus-draft probability-difference surrogate let GCG solve small fixed-candidate tasks, but not reliably generalize across large prompt spaces, despite successful black-box suffixes. This limits the tested optimizer/objective, not white-box attacks in principle. High A/B accuracy does not establish arbitrary prompt or PII recovery; two-topic simulated conversations remain restricted, and website tests exclude short responses. Improved Claude and website attacks use packet size as well as timing. Different underlying models confound rankings of inference methods. Release date is only a crude optimization proxy, and infrastructure changes versus workload changes remain competing explanations for signature decay. Constant-rate defense claims concern the evaluated timing channel, not every possible side channel.
coverage_notes: Repeated records represent one project. One passage says five of eight identified methods had reproduced public implementations, while supplied text is inconsistent about integrated method counts/names; algorithm-based vulnerability predictions must remain distinct from experiments. The draft model is inconsistently called 1.5B and 2B. The reported 91-call arithmetic is not fully explained. Explicit website topic figures are 79% and 82%, not uniformly over 80%. No unrelated-user interception or verified knowledge of proprietary inference algorithms is demonstrated.
